words: Tools, fasteners, and similar store goods
Device secured or released with a door key

Material such as iron or copper

Plain key piece before its teeth are cut

answerNotes.KEY: A door key is shaped to match a particular lock. A spare is another key kept for use if the main one is unavailable.
answerNotes.HARDWARE: A hardware store sells tools and practical supplies. A key blank can be cut there to match the shape of an existing key.
answerNotes.LOCK: A lock restricts access until the correct key or code is used. A latch holds a door closed without necessarily locking it.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is a raised work or serving surface. In a shop it separates the customer area from the worker's space.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.

title: Choosing a Card at the Gift Shop
subtheme: Choosing a Card at the Gift Shop
description: Choose a printed greeting and a matching envelope for a friend.
cardDescription: Choose a printed greeting and a matching envelope for a friend.
focus: The setting is choosing a Card at the Gift Shop. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Piece of stiff paper carrying a message
Yearly celebration of the day someone was born
Material used for writing or wrapping

answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.THANKS: Thanks expresses gratitude. The feeding story includes giving thanks before food is distributed.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.
answerNotes.GIFT: A gift is something given, rather than sold. A tag identifies the recipient; wrapping protects or decorates the present.
answerNotes.PRICE: Price is the amount asked for an item. Change is money returned after a customer pays more than that amount.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.

subtheme: A Parcel at the Shipping Counter

cardDescription: Weigh a securely wrapped parcel and add its destination label.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Wrapped package ready to give or send
Container with a base and sides
Sticky strip used to fasten paper
Location written on a mailed envelope
Send a package to another place
Flat shop surface used for transactions

answerNotes.PARCEL: A parcel is a wrapped package prepared for delivery. Labeling and secure wrapping help keep its address and contents together.
answerNotes.SCALE: A scale measures weight. Its reading is different from a price, although a shop may calculate price using that weight.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.TAPE: Adhesive tape fastens surfaces with a sticky strip. Magnetic recording tape is a different material sharing the same short name.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: An address tells where mail should go. The recipient's name identifies the person, while the street, city, and postal code locate the destination.
answerNotes.WRAP: Wrap means put a covering around something. Paper is common for parcels and shop goods, while cloth can also be a wrapping material.
answerNotes.STRING: String is a thin cord used for tying or flying a kite. A kite's string connects the flying frame to the person holding it.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is a raised work or serving surface. In a shop it separates the customer area from the worker's space.
answerNotes.RECEIPT: A receipt records a completed payment. A bill asks for payment, so the two papers serve different purposes.

answerNotes.FRAME: An eyeglass frame supports both lenses. Its bridge rests over the nose, and its arms extend toward the ears.
answerNotes.EAR: Ears receive sound. In an animal clue, the word usually asks for a body part rather than a call or other sound.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.MIRROR: A mirror reflects light to form an image. Cleaning the surface removes marks; it does not change the reflected object.

answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.BRUSH: A brush holds many bristles in one handle. Their width and stiffness affect the marks or cleaning action it makes.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.STIR: Stir means move a utensil through a mixture. It combines ingredients without necessarily beating in much air.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
